snippet: Keith Grover's iVoterGuide survey responses: Under what circumstances should abortion be allowed? Answer: 'Cases involving pregnancy by incest or rape; when the life or health of the woman is adjudged by competent medical authority to be in serious jeopardy; or when the fetus is known by competent medical authority to have severe defects that will not allow the baby to survive beyond birth.' On whether abortion providers should receive government funds: Strongly Agrees they should not receive federal, state, or local funding. Stated: 'Taxpayer dollars should never be used for abortion procedures.'

Senator Keith Grover's statement on HB261 Equal Opportunity Initiatives: 'In Utah, we're dedicated to equal opportunity and student success. We believe campuses should embrace viewpoint diversity, academic freedom, freedom of expression and institutional political neutrality. This bill will ensure institutions remain neutral on political issues, while students and faculty are able to express their opinions freely.' Grover served as the Senate floor sponsor of this bill banning DEI trainings, programs, and offices at public institutions.

State Senate lawmakers approved HB261 on Thursday with a 23-6 party-line vote. The bill, which overwrites diversity, equity and inclusion programs at public institutions, now heads to the House for a concurrence vote before going to Governor Spencer Cox, who is expected to sign it into law. Floor sponsor Sen. Keith Grover, R-Provo, emphasized the bill's purpose during Wednesday's debate: 'The reason we're doing this now is because it needs to happen. We need to now start providing equality of opportunity for all students.' Grover highlighted the bill's student success centers as its most important component.

The seven senators voting for the bill, all Republicans, were Stuart Adams, Lincoln Fillmore, Keith Grover, John Johnson McKell, Ann Millner and Jerry Stevenson. The Senate education committee voted 7-2 to advance House Bill 215, the Utah Fits All bill that would let students use public funds for private education.

Supports those who complete proper immigration screening procedures and have been 'appropriately screened' through proper legal proceedings.

On vaccine mandates: Responds 'Never' regarding government or employer vaccine requirements under any circumstances.

Keith Grover's iVoterGuide survey responses on taxes and budget: Supports 'continued regimens to look for greater efficiency' in the tax system. States: 'In Utah we have a surplus. Spending should not increase and unneeded tax dollars should be returned to the taxpayer.' Strongly disagrees that taxpayer-funded education should extend through college.

Keith Grover sponsored SB 236 (2026) titled 'Property Tax Exemption Process Amendments,' which was signed by the Governor on March 23, 2026. This bill addresses property tax exemption processes in Utah.

Senator Keith Grover (R - District 23) voted YES on SB332 (Artificial Intelligence Revisions) on February 28, 2025 (2nd reading) and March 3, 2025 (3rd reading). The bill extended Utah's AI Policy Act until July 1, 2027. It passed with 25 YES votes, 0 NO votes in the Senate, and was signed into law March 25, 2025.

SB 332 extended Utah's Artificial Intelligence Policy Act, which 'was scheduled to sunset on May 7, 2025, until July 1, 2027.' Related Utah 2025 AI laws included SB 226, which narrows the state's AI disclosure requirements, and HB 452, which imposes disclosure and advertising restrictions on mental health chatbots with penalties up to $2,500 per violation. These laws maintain a framework of disclosure requirements and accountability rather than imposing comprehensive AI bans.
